newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOODY'S AUSTRALIA SAYS MORTGAGED BACK ISSUES VARY.
newsitem.headline: MOODY'S AUSTRALIA SAYS MORTGAGED BACK ISSUES VARY.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday that credit risks for subordinated mortgage backed securities may very significantly, contrary to the belief of many Australian investors.
In a special report, Moody's stressed the importance of subordinated investors understanding all risks.

"They should always be concerned about the potential credit risks and structural risks but with the understanding that properly structured subordinated securities will still be eligible for high ratings," Moody's analysts Patrick Eng and Brian Cahill said in the report.
The analysts said that while the number of subordinated securities in Australia's mortgage backed securities (MBS) market had grown, so have their differences.
Moody's said it believed it was imperative investors make a careful distinction between, and a comparison of, the credit loss protections available in MBS securities.

"One unique feature of Australian mortgage back securities is the presence of mortgage insurance polices. However, this form of credit enhancement can give MBS investors a false sense of security," the report said.
